CanonicalVars.maps_to: _power_amount = 5 declared; the IncrementAmount var is not (colorless_powers.py:305)
CanonicalVars.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 24.) All 23 cards now store their printed C# var under a `_`-attribute (or, for 3 cards whose C# var is a live/computed value at display time -- guilty, normality, expect_a_fight -- a `magic_number` property override; wither similarly overrides `base_damage`) so `Card.base_damage`/`base_block`/`base_hp_loss`/`magic_number` report the C# value instead of the 0/None default. Two additive base.py changes: `_frail` added to `_MAGIC_ATTRS` (shame) and a new `base_gold` property (debt, spoils_map -- GoldVar had no base property at all). feel_no_pain's `_block` was renamed to `_power_amount` (fixing a WRONG value, not just a missing one -- `base_block` no longer misreports it as block-granting; matches Rage/Corruption/Stampede's DynamicVar('Power', ...) convention). Combat behavior / dealt numbers are byte-identical in every case -- a printed-number / observation-encoder fix only. 3 of the 23 (debt, spoils_map, rolling_boulder's secondary IncrementAmount) have NO obs-vector change despite the API fix (full_env.py has no base_gold read site; magic_number carries one number per card and _power_amount dominates rolling_boulder's scan) -- documented, not closed further. CHECKPOINT NOTE for training: encoded VALUES changed for the other 20 cards in feature slots f[17]/f[18] damage, f[20]/f[21] block, f[22] hp_loss, f[23] magic_number; obs LAYOUT unchanged. Pins: test/test_printed_vars.py (48 tests).  The text it replaced read: `new PowerVar<RollingBoulderPower>(5m)` maps to `_power_amount = 5`, but the second var `new DynamicVar("IncrementAmount", 5m)` (RollingBoulder.cs:17-21, mirrored by the `public const int incrementAmount = 5`) has no `_`-attribute -- the sim leaves the per-turn growth entirely to RollingBoulderPower. The APPLIED amount is right and the power's growth is the power stream's to audit; what is missing is the printed second number, so `magic_number` reports the starting 5 and nothing tells the observation encoder that it grows. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed number the sim's `magic_number` cannot surface, so `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card without it. DORMANT for game fidelity, LIVE for the observation encoder.

OnPlay.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<RollingBoulderPower>(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars["RollingBoulderPower"].IntValue, Owner.Creature, this)` (RollingBoulder.cs:30) == `PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, RollingBoulderPower, self._power_amount, applier=ctx.player)`. No animation on either side.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars["RollingBoulderPower"].UpgradeValueBy(5m)` (RollingBoulder.cs:35) == `self._power_amount += 5` (5 -> 10). The IncrementAmount stays 5 when upgraded -- only the STARTING damage doubles, which is the distinction the missing var would have made visible.
